copy.headline: Tarrant County College removes 4 courses from core offerings starting fall 2028
copy.caption:
The eliminated courses are not being discontinued and will remain active in TCC’s catalog and available for enrollment. Tarrant County College students will have four fewer options to meet core class requirements starting in fall 2028.

Trustees voted 6-0 on Nov. 19 to remove environmental biology, film appreciation and two Mexican American history courses from the college’s core curriculum requirements. The courses will remain available to students.

story.title: Tarrant County College removes 4 courses from core offerings starting fall 2028
story.summary: The eliminated courses are not being discontinued and will remain active in TCC’s catalog and available for enrollment. Tarrant County College students will have four fewer options to meet core class requirements starting in fall 2028. Trustees voted 6-0 on Nov. 19 to remove environmental biology, film appreciation and two Mexican American history courses from the college’s core curriculum requirements. The courses will remain available to students. Trustee Teresa Ayala was absent. TCC reviewed its 84 core courses and found that all core courses met state curriculum requirements. But the college’s core curriculum advisory committee recommended removing the courses because of low student demand, said Zarina Blankenbaker, vice chancellor for student success.
